source_text: (??)να δὲ ἤδη καὶ τοῦτο φανερὸν ὑμῖν γένηται, ὅτι, ὁπόσα λέγομεν μαθόντες παρὰ τοῦ Χριστοῦ, καὶ τῶν προελθόντων αὐτοῦ προφητῶν μόνα ἀληθῆ ἐστι καὶ πρεσβύτερα πάντων τῶν γεγενημένων συγγραφέων, καὶ οὐχὶ διὰ τὸ ταὐτὰ λέγειν αὐτοῖς παραδεχθῆναι ἀξιοῦμεν, ἀλλ᾿ ὅτι τὸ ἀληθὲς λέγομεν· καὶ Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς μόνος ἰδίως υἱὸς τῷ θεῷ γεγέννηται, λόγος αὐτοῦ ὑπάρχων καὶ πρωτότοκος καὶ δύναμις, καὶ τῇ βουλῇ αὐτοῦ γενόμενος ἄνθρωπος ταῦτα ἡμᾶς ἐδίδαξεν ἐπ᾿ ἀλλαγῇ καὶ ἐπαναγωγῇ τοῦ ἀνθρωπείου γένους· καὶ πρὶν ἢ ἐν ἄνθρωποις αὐτὸν γενέσθαι ἄνθρωπον φθάσαντές τινες, λέγω δὲ τοὺς προειρημένους κακοὺς δαίμονας, διὰ τῶν ποιητῶν ὡς γενόμενα εἶπον ἃ μυθοποιήσαντες ἔφησαν, ὃν τρόπον καὶ τὰ καθ᾿ ἡμῶν λεγόμενα δύσφημα καὶ ἀσεβῆ ἔργα ἐνήργησαν, ὤν οὐδεὶς μάρτυς οὐδὲ ἀπόδειξίς ἐστι, — τοῦτον ἔλεγχον ποιησόμεθα.¦
pass_a_gloss: But let this also become clear to you, that whatever we say, having learned from Christ and the prophets who came before Him, are the only true and older than all the writers who have existed; and we do not ask to be accepted because we say the same things as them, but because we say the truth; and Jesus Christ, uniquely the Son of God, has been born, being His Word and firstborn and power, and having become a man by His will, He taught us these things for the transformation and restoration of the human race; and before He became a man among men, certain ones, I say the aforementioned evil demons, having anticipated, spoke through the poets the things they had mythologized as having happened, in the same way that they also brought about the evil and impious deeds that are spoken against us, of which there is no witness or proof - we will make a refutation of this.

choices.why: accurate rendering of the Greek prepositions
accurate rendering of the Greek genitive phrase

pass_b_english: Let this also become clear to you: whatever we say, having learned it from Christ and the prophets who preceded him, is alone true and older than every writer who has ever existed. We do not ask to be accepted because we say the same things they do, but because we speak the truth. Jesus Christ has been begotten as the unique Son of God; he is God's Word, firstborn, and power. By the Father's will he became a man and taught us these things for the transformation and restoration of the human race. Before he became a man among men, certain ones — I mean the evil demons already mentioned — anticipated him and spoke through the poets the myths they had fabricated, just as they also brought about the slanderous and impious deeds spoken against us, for which there is neither witness nor proof. We will refute this charge.

anf_compare.notes: Drafted from source only; ANF not shown to drafter.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the complex syntax of the Greek, including the parenthetical remark regarding the demons and the distinction between the source of truth and the reason for acceptance. Pass B correctly identifies 'τῇ βουλῇ αὐτοῦ' as 'By the Father's will' (interpreting the reflexive/divine will contextually) or 'his will', and 'δύσφημα' as 'slanderous'. Pass A is also a faithful rendering.
